problem: Mobile construction robots assume task locations are predefined (coordinates or BIM). Prior LLM/LMM navigation works also handle only simple object search, cannot handle attribute or contextual conditions, and process commands one-directionally, so they cannot accept mid-execution changes.
motivation: Construction tasks, both direct and auxiliary work, are often improvisational: the location, instruction and timing are not known in advance. Robots that cannot position themselves for such tasks contribute little. Drawings give coarse zone information while fine, non-static targets need visual reasoning.
key_idea: Split the agent into three parallel GPT-4o modules (agent core for task breakdown, drawing-based zone navigation, and vision-based fine positioning) so a quadruped can position itself at unknown, condition-specified locations while accepting mid-execution commands.
insight: Coarse zone navigation from construction drawings plus direct LMM visual reasoning for fine positioning handles attribute and contextual conditions. In the Test B comparison, this gave 86.7% target identification versus 26.7% and 33.3% for open-vocabulary detectors (Grounding DINO, YOLOv8x-world) that pick the highest-confidence box. Parallel modules with a task runner and stop signal let mid-execution edits work: all 8 failures came from navigation or positioning (1 navigation, 7 positioning) and none from the agent core. The main failure mode is weak LMM spatial and visual grounding, plus latency from API calls.
method: Agent core: GPT-4o reasoning called only when a new command arrives; generates or modifies a task list, splitting each command into a zone-level location and a detailed task instruction; a task memory holds the list

Task runner: an async loop parallel to LMM reasoning; pops tasks, sends the zone to the navigation module and the instruction to the positioning module; proceeds only if navigation succeeds; on modification sends a stop signal to both modules and reissues the task

Navigation module (preparation): YOLO plus EasyOCR detect and read zone labels on the drawing PNG; labels are converted to map coordinates in meters; the LMM writes a text description per label location, saved as JSON

Navigation module (destination and checking): exact labels are used directly; semantic phrases such as 'south hallway' or 'center between 12C1 and 12C2' are resolved by the LMM over the JSON; the goal goes to ROS2 Nav2/SLAM; monitors position and runs a LiDAR-based recovery if navigation stops abnormally

Positioning module: GPT-4o receives the camera image (with left/center/right visual prompting), the task instruction and LiDAR forward clearance; outputs reasoning, direction (left/right/center/not visible) and distance (too far/too close/appropriate/not visible); maps these to short actions (forward/back 25 cm, turn 15°, look around 40°) until center and appropriate; target range 0.5-0.8 m

System implementation: Unitree Go2 with Jetson Orin Nano running ROS and video containers; 8 Docker containers on the server (3 LMM modules, 4 tools, UI); gRPC between containers, TCP to robot, HTTP to UI

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen, via API) for all three modules; YOLO + EasyOCR for label reading
setting.observation: monocular RGB camera on Go2, LiDAR forward clearance and SLAM pose, construction drawing image plus ROS binary grid map
setting.action_space: Nav2 goal coordinates for zone-level navigation; low-level moves: forward/back 25 cm, turn 15°, look around 40°
setting.privileged: preloaded construction drawing with zone labels and a pre-built ROS occupancy grid map; no GT object locations

numbers.extra: preloaded drawing and occupancy map; success = face target, within 1 m, agent self-judges success

results: Across 45 real-robot sessions (103 tasks) the agent reached 92.2% task SR and 82.2% session SR, with 93.9% and 86.7% in the hardest Test C (mid-execution commands). In the target-identification comparison it scored 86.7% versus 26.7% (Grounding DINO) and 33.3% (YOLOv8x-world).
limitations: Tested only in a controlled indoor office, not on real construction sites; needs a preloaded drawing and occupancy map
Positioning failures from LMM weakness in visual grounding and spatial reasoning (7 of 8 failures); relies on GPT-4o API, so about 2 minutes per task
Small test scale (15 sessions per test, 15-task baseline comparison) and no comparison against other LMM navigation agents
